edit.description: Early same-clock historical forecasts, smoothly approach frozen static teachers
edit.interpolation: smoothstep; phase is normalized over observed score nodes; no extrapolation
edit.normalization: dose is normalized over actual score nodes to a mean of one

failure_modes: Affinity: the reward is an empirical post-native control, not an exact tilted-density sample; improved predicted target affinity is not established by the coordinate contrast alone, and decoded final affinity is unobserved in this handoff.

Strain/validity: graph changes are permitted, but coordinate similarity does not establish improved affinity; strain and structural validity must be reported separately and could degrade even if the endpoint contrast tracks the schedule.

Gradient cancellation: the observed-to-static blend can produce opposing component gradients; a changing scalar reward value does not prove changed injection, so gradient-direction and delivered-dose checks are required to distinguish cancellation from an unsuitable target.

Timing attribution: a benefit must be attributable to timing, so S1 must be compared against S2 (constant blend) and S3 (time-order control) at fixed dose; otherwise the effect could be a generic blend effect.

Support: only one of 200 curve features was read and no stage/temporal profiles exist, so no data-derived knot or cross-feature conclusion is supported; the phase knot at 0.5 is an experimental hypothesis, not a discovered stage.
rationale: H001 states the landmark_00_soft_mass endpoint contrast reverses sign within the observed score window [0.0,0.49] (rise to a peak near t=0.16, then decline; 4 sign changes, 1 strong sign conflict, cubic not accepted, extrapolation disallowed), so a fixed endpoint target is mis-specified over the full support. The registered reward-lane recipe S1_observed_to_static keeps dose_factors=1 and delta=1 while smoothly shifting relevance from early same-clock historical forecasts toward frozen static teachers, which matches a reversing contrast better than a constant blend (S2) or the opposite-order control (S3). S1 is the offered choice whose schedule is consistent with the observed reversal; S2 and S3 remain the constant-blend and time-order controls for attribution.
